cands.name: Phil Rubin
cands.bio: Phil Rubin is a Democrat and attorney who represents North Carolina House District 40. Gov. Josh Stein appointed him in January 2025 to replace Joe John. He was previously an Assistant U.S. Attorney, a Special Deputy Attorney General in North Carolina, and an online child-safety policy worker.
cands.gaps: His birthplace, where he grew up, and when he moved to North Carolina are not in the sources we could read. The sources give no dates for his legal jobs. We found no statements or actions from him on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, limits on foreign or investor land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, abortion, or police pay and pensions. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored was empty on the page we read, so we could not confirm any specific bill. His campaign site says he is primary sponsor of the Fair Maps Act, but we found no legislative record of it.

qual.background: He has served in the NC House since January 2025. Before that he was an Assistant U.S. Attorney (Eastern District of NC), a Special Deputy Attorney General, a Covington & Burling attorney, and a clerk to Chief Judge David Sentelle of the D.C. Circuit. He also worked in online child safety.
qual.why: He has legislative service, though only about two years, plus a long legal and public-policy career. That puts him in the high band, but short of the top because his time in the chamber is brief and no leadership role is documented.

cands.name: Lucas Everett Jones
cands.bio: Libertarian candidate for North Carolina House District 40 in 2026. Ballotpedia lists no occupation, offices held or biography for him.

He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign website, interviews or questionnaires with his positions. We found nothing on his stance toward data centers, development, taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. We found no news coverage of controversies or foreign ties.
